sections.title: The Ghosn Intelligence Channel
sections.content:
The Karp-Epstein correspondence on the Carlos Ghosn arrest constitutes the most granular evidence of bidirectional intelligence brokering in the DOJ email corpus. The channel activated instantly: Karp told Epstein he was "dealing with Ghosn crisis" on November 20, 2018, the day after the arrest (EFTA02616157). Within ten days, Epstein offered intelligence from his own source: "ghosen info when you like." Karp's reply — "That was quick. On call with DOJ now" — confirms two things simultaneously: that Karp was briefing the Department of Justice on Ghosn-related matters, and that he recognized the speed with which Epstein had obtained information (EFTA02612503). Epstein's response, comparing his source to "the experienced mechanic" who knows "exactly where to knock," suggests a targeted intelligence asset rather than general media monitoring.

The exchange on December 26, 2018, is the most consequential. Epstein wrote: "following ghosen. it appears my guy had it right from day one. any updates?" Karp, returning from Tokyo, validated the source: "Just returning from tokyo. Your guy totally had it right" (EFTA02609103). Karp's Christmas-period trip to Tokyo in his capacity as Paul Weiss chairman underscores the seniority of the firm's involvement in the Ghosn matter. Four days later, Epstein followed up: "how you doing? traveling to tokyo must have been stressful" (EFTA02608327). The informality of these exchanges — checking in on the stress of international travel, sharing intelligence assessments in casual fragments — reflects a relationship in which the chairman of a major law firm routinely confirmed or denied the accuracy of a convicted sex offender's independent intelligence on an ongoing DOJ matter.

The channel culminated in late January 2019. On January 24, Epstein told Karp: "when free I can bring you up to date on google. ghosen SIC and..." (EFTA02626821) — offering updates on multiple matters at once, including one involving Google and the ongoing Ghosn situation. Two days later, on January 26, Epstein wrote "ghosen a very very not good guy" and pivoted immediately: "Rajeev misra do you represent?" (EFTA02627034). Karp confirmed: "Sort of. Spoke to him yesterday." Epstein then clarified to a third party: "brad represent softbank, not rajeev, but did speak to him yesterday, re DB" — revealing that Karp had also discussed Deutsche Bank matters with Rajeev Misra. The same day, Reid Weingarten independently asked Epstein about Misra, creating a dual-channel intelligence operation in which Epstein brokered information between Karp (representing SoftBank) and Weingarten (seeking intelligence on Misra) without either knowing the full picture.

sections.title: Leon Black and the Apollo Exposure
sections.content:
Karp's relationship with Leon Black through Epstein created overlapping professional and personal obligations that are difficult to disentangle. In March 2016, Karp forwarded to Epstein a Paul Weiss internal exchange about Black's request to establish a $2 million escrow fund at the firm "from which payments would be made monthly pursuant to a contract with an individual" (EFTA02470157). Paul Weiss partner Bruce Birenboim declined to serve as escrow agent, but the episode reveals Karp as the transmission point between Black's financial requests and Epstein's operational infrastructure. A November 2016 three-way billing email among Karp, Epstein, and Black addressed which party was paying for Paul Weiss, Akin Gump, Deloitte, and PwC services — demonstrating that the advisory fee structures were intertwined rather than cleanly separated.

When Epstein discovered in August 2016 that all three Apollo co-founders — Black, Joshua Harris, and Marc Rowan — had failed to properly file IRS Form 8865 for the BRH Holdings foreign partnership, it was Karp at Paul Weiss whom Epstein contacted. Karp's response: "First I have heard of this." The 8865 compliance failure carried open statutes of limitation extending back to 2007, and Steven Pesner at Akin Gump was placed on the advisory team alongside Karp. In August 2016, Epstein separately emailed Karp: "is Caesars getting better or worse?" (EFTA02452879). At that time, Paul Weiss was counsel to CEC and Apollo in the CEOC restructuring and was a named defendant in Case 15-01145, which alleged the firm simultaneously represented Apollo, CEC, and CEOC while engineering fraudulent asset transfers. A court-appointed examiner found Paul Weiss had a conflict of interest. For Karp to discuss even the general trajectory of the Caesars litigation with Epstein — a non-party with no privilege claim — represents a potential breach of attorney-client confidentiality that predates the Ghosn intelligence leaks by more than two years.

Karp also served as a conduit for Epstein's advisory network around Marc Rowan. Epstein engaged Karp to work on Apollo/Athene restructuring matters, with Ruemmler recommending hires at Paul Weiss in connection with the work (EFTA02386047). The Caesars breach, the 8865 crisis, the Black escrow, and the Rowan advisory all demonstrate a pattern in which Karp served not merely as Paul Weiss's chairman but as Epstein's primary institutional contact within the firm — routing work, sharing intelligence, and bridging what should have been firewalled client relationships.

sections.title: The Weingarten Shadow Advisory

sections.title: Surveillance and Private Intelligence
sections.content:

On March 30, 2019 — less than four months before Epstein's final arrest — Epstein asked Karp: "is your go to investigators kroll?" The phrasing "these types of matters" is ambiguous but significant: it implies Karp had discussed with Epstein the specific nature of the investigation for which Epstein was seeking resources, and had rendered a professional judgment about which firm was best suited. Nardello & Co., founded by former federal prosecutor Daniel Nardello, is a corporate intelligence firm specializing in due diligence, asset tracing, and litigation support.

The investigation database records that Karp coordinated Nardello surveillance in connection with Leon Black's dispute with Guzel Ganieva in 2015 (EFTA02384875). sections.title: The Ghosn Lobbying Architecture
sections.content:

The firm held five FARA registrations between 1963 and 2002, representing the governments of Israel, Morocco, Poland, and Botswana, as well as Japanese and Korean corporations including NEC (1982–1996), Samsung, Hyundai, and Korea Telecom. The NEC representation gave Paul Weiss more than a decade of institutional knowledge of Japanese corporate and legal systems — directly relevant to Karp's December 2018 Tokyo trip. Yet none of these FARA registrations were active during the Karp-Epstein period, and the Ghosn engagement was never registered as foreign agent activity. This regulatory arbitrage — using domestic lobbying registration for what was functionally a foreign advocacy campaign — is consistent with the broader pattern of FARA non-compliance documented across the Epstein network.
